title: Siena R4794 (unnumbered): a slip wholly in cipher on pieces of artillery, 16th century

steps.what: Project survey (siena1421): transcription r4794.txt and homsolve.py annealing; no key found, closed as too short.
Transcription by Claude, refined by George Lasry in CTTS.
CTTS built-in cryptanalysis gave an initial key of 23 values.
Claude corrected and completed the key with crib guessing and dragging; the frame-plus-dot grid structure recognised.
Whole slip deciphered; the four number codes unidentified; two encipherer slips corrected.
Report key figures of nos. 5, 15 and 17 compared sign by sign: a different key from both.

R4794: his key on the project's own 24 Sept transcription (project_attempt/r4794.txt): 83.8% (134/160); his key table has no H and no R column though his reading has h 7 times and r 11 times; our A aligns with r every time and our N with h; with those two values added, 93.1% (149/160). research/siena2308/verify_lasry.py r4794, r4794b.

validation.notes: contributed reading: George Lasry's sign-level CTTS transcription and key are not in the repository, so no token alignment can be scored

outcome.method_basis: The report says CTTS cryptanalysis gave 23 values from the ciphertext and Claude completed the key by crib dragging; the slip has no clear text and no key fits.
outcome.fraction_read_source: George Lasry's counts in the report: all 160 letter signs have a value; the 5 number-code tokens (26 twice, 44, 67, 74) are unidentified; 160/165 cipher symbols

gaps.detail: The nomenclator is lost; no key in the busta fits the slip.

credits.note: Key recovered ciphertext-only with CTTS and Claude; decipherment and translation (report pp. 31-32).
credits.source: Email and report to Daniel Bourdeau, 17 Oct 2026

prior.where: None known; the project's 24 Sept survey left it unread.

human: Claude transcribed, George Lasry refined in CTTS; CTTS cryptanalysis gave 23 values, completed by Claude with crib guessing and dragging. This project filed his report.
